blocks.x: Omnichannel fulfillment on governed agents, click-and-collect SLA at 96% and store labor hours on fulfillment down 31%

A home-improvement retailer: Retail chains feel decision gaps in margin per store, visible in the weekly numbers. The Achala program started with the pricing and availability flow —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.
The baseline month timed the promise: 84% click-and-collect within SLA, pickers wandering a 140,000-SKU floor with a list and a prayer, and mis-picks that turned the promise into an apology queue.
Store inventory accuracy was the real constraint: system said 4, floor said 2. Every pick was a small treasure hunt, and the labor plan assumed the hunt was free.

We moved fulfillment to governed agents: orders slotted to stores on real availability with substitution logic signed by merchandising, pick paths optimized with location-accuracy weighting, discrepancy loops feeding the inventory record in near real time, and labor forecasting reading the actual pick workload. The apology queue emptied; the labor plan started believing the data.
